children: New U.S. chip export controls may introduce fresh uncertainties for Malaysia data center-related tenders, potentially slowing contract awards as customers adopt a wait-and-see approach, CIMB Securities analysts Kenny Mak Hoy Ken and Wei Yi Tan say in a note. However, most Malaysian listed contractors have limited direct exposure to projects involving D5-country entities, reducing the risk of project cancellation, they say. The controls could also delay grid connection projects as compliance requirements slow customer onboarding and capacity deployment, they add. A slower U.S. data center buildout could redirect AI infrastructure investment to Asean, with Malaysia standing out for its neutral geopolitical position and maturing data center ecosystem. CIMB maintains a neutral rating on Malaysia's construction and materials sector, pegging Gamuda as top pick given its diversified earnings.(yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
